subject: Packaging alignment: upgrade/downgrade paths, feature bundling, and SKU prioritization
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@meditrek.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@meditrek.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question — upgrade/downgrade flexibility and bundling

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking a look. We're in the final evaluation phase for inference at MediTrek and have a couple of packaging questions that matter for procurement and our engineering roadmap:

- We expect bursty usage (30–60% of tokens in monthly bursts). How hard is it to move between tiers mid-contract (downgrade if usage drops)? Any proration or credit mechanics we should expect?
- We need clarity on feature bundling: can we buy the core throughput tier and opt into specific add-ons (private VPC, extended observability) incrementally?
- Pricing: do you support a laddered discount if committed throughput increases mid-term, or do we need a contract amendment?

I've attached a short requirements PDF (meditrek_requirements.pdf) and marked the areas where flexibility matters for us. Would appreciate a quick rundown and an example scenario (e.g., 200M tokens/month baseline, 600M token burst months).

Would it help to loop in your pricing/solutions folks? Happy to schedule 30 minutes.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Strategy
MediTrek

--
Attachment: meditrek_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@meditrek.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — upgrade/downgrade flexibility and bundling

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear requirements doc. Quick answers up front, then a suggested next step:

- Downgrade/upgrade mechanics: we support mid-term tier moves. Downgrades are governed by a 30-day notice for seat/throughput reallocation; credits are provided on a prorated basis for committed capacity, but feature-licensed add-ons (e.g., Private deployment) are billed on a prorated subscription model and may have a short minimum term.
- Bundling: yes — core throughput + incremental add-ons is our standard model. Add-ons can be toggled with a 30-day lead; some security/compliance add-ons (KMS/HSM integrations) require a setup window and may incur a one-time integration fee.
- Discounts: laddered discounts are possible via a contract amendment (we can auto-escalate discount bands if committed throughput crosses thresholds), or we can provide a staged pricing schedule up front to avoid amendments.

I attached a simple mapping worksheet (draft_pack_map.xlsx) that shows a baseline + burst example and two downgrade flows. Can you confirm the burst cadence (months/year) and target post-burst baseline? That will let us propose either a staged discount or a flexible commit with burst buffers.

If you want, I can bring Ben (pricing) and Karthik (solutions) into a 30-min call tomorrow. Proposed times: 10:00 or 15:30 PT. Which works?

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Growth Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: draft_pack_map.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@meditrek.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — upgrade/downgrade flexibility and bundling

Sanjay —

Jumping in with concrete pricing scenarios attached (scenario_pricing.csv). High level:

Scenario A — Standard Commit
- Baseline: 200M tokens/month (committed) + 100M burst buffer.
- Monthly unit price: $0.0009/token (hosted) after 10% contract discount.
- Downgrade: allowed after 90 days with prorated credit (applied to next invoice).

Scenario B — Elastic Commit (recommended for bursty workloads)
- Baseline: 150M tokens/month committed; 400M burst-capacity billed at usage tiers (higher per-token but no contract amendment).
- Monthly unit price: baseline @ $0.00085/token (15% discount), burst @ $0.00110/token.
- Laddered discount: if 3-month rolling average > 400M tokens, baseline rate automatically steps down 2%.

Add-ons pricing (monthly):
- Private VPC: $10,000/month (one-time setup $7,500)
- Extended Observability (90-day retention): $4,000/month
- SLA uplift (99.95%): +12% on baseline commit cost

We can also include a one-time migration credit applied to the first three months if you sign a 12-month commit (negotiable). See scenario_pricing.csv for math.

If you confirm target baseline after burst months, we can draft a 1-page commercial summary for procurement.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@meditrek.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — upgrade/downgrade flexibility and bundling

Ben, Hannah —

Thanks — the two scenarios are helpful. A few clarifications from procurement/finance:

1) For Scenario B (Elastic Commit): can you confirm whether the laddered 2% stepdown is retrospective (applied to prior invoices) or prospective only? Procurement prefers prospective adjustments to avoid crediting back months.
2) If we take the 12-month commit w/ migration credit, what level of flexibility do we have at month 6 to reduce baseline by up to 25%? We'd accept a modest break fee, but want predictable proration mechanics.
3) Private VPC setup: can you confirm the integration window (workdays) and whether the setup fee is refundable if integration is delayed?

We're leaning to Scenario B but need granular proration language for legal. Also, Lauren — are you able to share any standard contract language around mid-term adjustments?

Would prefer to lock something by the end of next week.

Best,
Sanjay

Subject: Re: Packaging question — upgrade/downgrade flexibility and bundling

Hi Sanjay —

Couple of operational notes from engineering/solutions to support the commercial asks:

- Downgrade practicality: reducing committed throughput is operationally straightforward. We recommend a 30-day notice window and a 90-day soft lock for cache/instance rightsizing to avoid instability. The proration credit is calculated on committed capacity only; burst usage billed as actuals. We'll put the exact formula in the commercial summary.
- Elastic Commit behavior: the 2% laddered stepdown we described is prospective (applies to subsequent billing cycles). To satisfy procurement, we can offer a hybrid: a one-time reconciliation credit capped at one month of baseline cost if the three-month average exceeds the threshold — this keeps reconciliation predictable.
- Private VPC setup: typical lead is 10–14 business days; setup fee is non-refundable but can be converted to a service credit if integration is delayed for reasons on our side. We'll capture that in the SOW.

I've put together a minimal commercial summary draft and scoping checklist in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cpackaging-docs — please review. If the harmonized terms look good, Hannah/Ben, can we produce a 1-page commercial for procurement by Monday?

-Karthik

Redwood Inference
